The '''Knaster–Kuratowski–Mazurkiewicz lemma''' is a basic result in mathematical [[fixed-point theorem|fixed-point theory]] published in 1929 by [[Bronisław Knaster|Knaster]], [[Kazimierz Kuratowski|Kuratowski]] and [[Stefan Mazurkiewicz|Mazurkiewicz]].<ref>{{citation|first1=B.|last1=Knaster|author1-link=Bronisław Knaster|first2=C.|last2=Kuratowski|author2-link=Kazimierz Kuratowski|first3=S.|last3=Mazurkiewicz|author3-link=Stefan Mazurkiewicz|title=Ein Beweis des Fixpunktsatzes für ''n''-dimensionale Simplexe|journal=[[Fundamenta Mathematicae]]|volume=14|issue=1|year=1929|pages=132–137|doi=10.4064/fm-14-1-132-137|language=de|url=https://eudml.org/doc/212127|doi-access=free}}.</ref>

The KKM lemma can be proved from [[Sperner's lemma]] and can be used to prove the [[Brouwer fixed-point theorem]].

==Statement==
Let <math>\Delta_{n-1}</math> be an <math>(n-1)</math>-dimensional [[simplex]] with ''n'' [[Vertex (geometry)|vertices]] labeled as <math>1,\ldots,n</math>.

A '''KKM covering''' is defined as a set <math>C_1,\ldots,C_n \subseteq \Delta_{n-1}</math> of [[closed sets|closed subsets]] of the simplex such that for any <math>I \subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}</math>, the [[convex hull]] of the vertices corresponding to <math>I</math> is [[Cover (topology)|covered]] by <math>\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i</math>.

The KKM lemma says that '''in every KKM covering, the common intersection of all ''n'' sets is nonempty''', i.e.:
:<math>\bigcap_{i=1}^n C_i \neq \emptyset.</math>
An equivalent way of stating the KKM lemma says that whenever <math>C_1,\ldots,C_n \subseteq \Delta_{n-1}</math> are closed subsets of the simplex such that every point <math>(x_1,\ldots,x_n) \in \Delta_{n-1}</math> belongs to some <math>C_i</math> for some index <math>i \in \{1, \dots, n\}</math> with <math>x_i > 0</math>, then there exists a point of <math>\Delta_{n-1}</math> that is in all sets simultaneously.<ref>{{cite arXiv | last1=Igarashi | first1=Ayumi | last2=Meunier | first2=Frédéric | title=Fair and efficient allocation of indivisible items under category constraints | date=2025 | class=cs.GT | eprint=2503.20260 }}</ref>

==Example==

When <math>n=3</math>, the KKM lemma considers the simplex <math>\Delta_2</math> which is a triangle, whose vertices can be labeled 1, 2 and 3.  We are given three closed sets <math>C_1,C_2,C_3</math> such that:
* <math>C_1</math> covers vertex 1, <math>C_2</math> covers vertex 2, <math>C_3</math> covers vertex 3.
* The edge 12 (from vertex 1 to vertex 2) is covered by the sets <math>C_1</math> and <math>C_2</math>, the edge 23 is covered by the sets <math>C_2</math> and <math>C_3</math>, the edge 31 is covered by the sets <math>C_3</math> and <math>C_1</math>.
* The union of all three sets covers the entire triangle
The KKM lemma states that the sets <math>C_1, C_2, C_3</math> have at least one point in common.

[[File:KKM example.png|thumb|An example of a covering satisfying the requirements of the KKM lemma]]

The lemma is illustrated by the picture on the right, in which set #1 is blue, set #2 is red and set #3 is green. The KKM requirements are satisfied, since:
* Each vertex is covered by a unique color.
* Each edge is covered by the two colors of its two vertices.
* The triangle is covered by all three colors.
The KKM lemma states that there is a point covered by all three colors simultaneously; such a point is clearly visible in the picture.

Note that it is important that all sets are closed, i.e., contain their boundary. If, for example, the red set is not closed, then it is possible that the central point is contained only in the blue and green sets, and then the intersection of all three sets may be empty.

== Generalizations ==
===<span class="anchor" id="rainbow"></span><span class="anchor" id="permutation"></span><span id='permutation'>Rainbow KKM lemma (Gale)</span>===
[[David Gale]] proved the following generalization of the KKM lemma.<ref name="g84">{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/BF01769865|title=Equilibrium in a discrete exchange economy with money|journal=International Journal of Game Theory|volume=13|pages=61–64|year=1984|last1=Gale|first1=D.|s2cid=154888988}}</ref> Suppose that, instead of one KKM covering, we have ''n'' different KKM coverings: <math>C^1_1,\ldots,C^1_n,\ldots,C^n_1,\ldots,C^n_n</math>. Then, there exists a permutation <math>\pi</math> of the coverings with a non-empty intersection, i.e.:
:<math>\bigcap_{i=1}^{n}C^{\pi(i)}_i \neq \emptyset</math>.

The name "rainbow KKM lemma" is inspired by Gale's description of his lemma:<blockquote>"A colloquial statement of this result is... if each of three people paint a triangle red, white and blue according to the KKM rules, then there will be a point which is in the red set of one person, the white set of another, the blue of the third".<ref name="g84" /></blockquote>The rainbow KKM lemma can be proved using a [[Sperner's lemma#rainbow|rainbow generalization of Sperner's lemma]].<ref name="b87">{{cite journal|last1=Bapat|first1=R. B.|author-link=Ravindra Bapat|year=1989|title=A constructive proof of a permutation-based generalization of Sperner's lemma|journal=Mathematical Programming|volume=44|issue=1–3|pages=113–120|doi=10.1007/BF01587081|s2cid=5325605}}</ref>

The original KKM lemma follows from the rainbow KKM lemma by simply picking ''n'' identical coverings.

===Connector-free lemma (Bapat)===
[[File:KKM generalized example.png|thumb|An illustration of the generalized KKM lemma by Bapat]]

A '''connector''' of a simplex is a [[connected set]] that touches all ''n'' faces of the simplex.

A '''connector-free covering''' is a covering <math>C_1,\ldots,C_n</math> in which no <math>C_i</math> contains a connector.

Any KKM covering is a connector-free covering, since in a KKM covering, no <math>C_i</math> even touches all ''n'' faces. However, there are connector-free coverings that are not KKM coverings. An example is illustrated at the right. There, the red set touches all three faces, but it does not contain any connector, since no connected component of it touches all three faces.

A theorem of [[Ravindra Bapat]], generalizing [[Sperner's lemma]],<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bapat|first1=Ravindra|title=Modeling, Computation and Optimization|date=2009-04-03|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=9789814467896|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yN7FCgAAQBAJ}}</ref>{{rp|chapter 16, pp. 257–261}} implies the KKM lemma extends to connector-free coverings (he proved his theorem for <math>n=3</math>).

The connector-free variant also has a permutation variant, so that both these generalizations can be used simultaneously.

=== <span class="anchor" id="KKMS"></span><span id='KKMS'>KKMS theorem</span> ===
The '''KKMS theorem''' is a generalization of the KKM lemma by [[Lloyd Shapley]]. It is useful in [[economics]], especially in [[cooperative game theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/BF01210576|title=On Kakutani's fixed point theorem, the K-K-M-S theorem and the core of a balanced game|journal=Economic Theory|volume=1|pages=108–116|year=1991|last1=Shapley|first1=Lloyd|last2=Vohra|first2=Rajiv|s2cid=121027709}}</ref>

While a KKM covering contains ''n'' closed sets, a '''KKMS covering''' contains <math>2^n-1</math> [[closed set]]s - indexed by the nonempty subsets of <math>[n]</math> (equivalently: by nonempty faces of <math>\Delta_{n-1}</math>). For any <math>I \subseteq [n]</math>, the [[convex hull]] of the vertices corresponding to <math>I</math> should be [[Cover (topology)|covered]] by the union of sets corresponding to subsets of <math>I</math> , that is: <blockquote><math>\operatorname{conv}(\{v_i : i\in I\}) \subseteq \bigcup_{J \subseteq I}C_J</math>. </blockquote>Any KKM covering is a special case of a KKMS covering. In a KKM covering, the ''n'' sets corresponding to singletons are nonempty, while the other sets are empty. However, there are many other KKMS coverings.

in general, it is ''not'' true that the common intersection of all <math>2^n-1</math> sets in a KKMS covering is nonempty; this is illustrated by the special case of a KKM covering, in which most sets are empty.

The KKMS theorem says that, '''in every KKMS covering, there is a ''balanced collection'' <math>B</math> of <math>2^{[n]}</math>, such that the intersection of sets indexed by <math>B</math> is nonempty''':<ref name="i81">{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0022-247X(81)90063-9|title=On the Knaster-Kuratowski-Mazurkiewicz-Shapley theorem|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|volume=81|issue=2|pages=297–299|year=1981|last1=Ichiishi|first1=Tatsuro|doi-access=free}}</ref>
:<math>\bigcap_{J\in B} C_J \neq \emptyset</math>

It remains to explain what a "balanced collection" is. A collection <math>B</math> of subsets of <math>[n]</math> is called ''balanced'' if there is a [[weight function]] on <math>B</math> (assigning a weight <math>w_J\geq 0</math> to every <math>J\in B</math>), such that, for each element <math>i\in [n]</math>, the sum of weights of all subsets containing <math>i</math> is exactly 1. For example, suppose <math>n=3</math>. Then:
* The collection <nowiki>{{1}, {2}, {3}}</nowiki> is balanced: choose all weights to be 1. The same is true for any collection in which each element appears exactly once, such as the collection <nowiki>{{1,2},{3}}</nowiki> or the collection { {1,2,3} }.
* The collection <nowiki>{{1,2}, {2,3}, {3,1}}</nowiki> is balanced: choose all weights to be 1/2. The same is true for any collection in which each element appears exactly twice.
* The collection <nowiki>{{1,2}, {2,3}}</nowiki> is not balanced, since for any choice of positive weights, the sum of weights for element 2 will be equal to the sum for element 1 or 3, so it is not possible that all sums equal 1.
* The collection <nowiki>{{1,2}, {2,3}, {1}}</nowiki> is balanced: choose <math>w_{1,2}=0,w_{2,3}=1,w_{1}=1</math>.

In [[Matching in hypergraphs|hypergraph terminology]], a collection ''B'' is balanced with respect to its ground-set ''V'', iff the hypergraph with vertex-set ''V'' and edge-set ''B'' admits a perfect fractional matching.

The KKMS theorem implies the KKM lemma.<ref name="i81" /> Suppose we have a KKM covering <math>C_i</math>, for <math>i=1,\ldots,n</math>. Construct a KKMS covering <math>C'_J</math> as follows:
*<math>C'_J = C_i</math> whenever <math>J=\{i\}</math> (<math>J</math> is a singleton that contains only element <math>i</math>).
*<math>C'_J = \emptyset</math> otherwise.
The KKM condition on the original covering <math>C_i</math> implies the KKMS condition on the new covering <math>C'_J</math>. Therefore, there exists a balanced collection such that the corresponding sets in the new covering have nonempty intersection. But the only possible balanced collection is the collection of all singletons; hence, the original covering has nonempty intersection.

The KKMS theorem has various proofs.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/BF01215384|title=An elementary proof of the Knaster-Kuratowski-Mazurkiewicz-Shapley Theorem|journal=Economic Theory|volume=4|issue=3|pages=467|year=1994|last1=Krasa|first1=Stefan|last2=Yannelis|first2=Nicholas C.|s2cid=15004516}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/BF01215383|title=A simple proof of K-K-M-S theorem|journal=Economic Theory|volume=4|issue=3|pages=463–466|year=1994|last1=Komiya|first1=Hidetoshi|s2cid=123150937}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/s001990050161|title=An extremely simple proof of the K-K-M-S Theorem|journal=Economic Theory|volume=10|issue=2|pages=361–367|year=1997|last1=Herings|first1=P. Jean-Jacques|s2cid=122754557}}</ref>

Reny and Wooders proved that the [[balanced set]] can also be chosen to be ''partnered''.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/S0304-4068(97)00004-9|title=An extension of the KKMS theorem|journal=Journal of Mathematical Economics|volume=29|issue=2|pages=125|year=1998|last1=Reny|first1=Philip J.|last2=Holtz Wooders|first2=Myrna}}</ref>

Zhou proved a variant of the KKMS theorem where the covering consists of [[open set]]s rather than closed sets.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Zhou|first=Lin|date=1994|title=A Theorem on Open Coverings of a Simplex and Scarf's Core Existence Theorem through Brouwer's Fixed Point Theorem|journal=Economic Theory|volume=4|issue=3|pages=473–477|doi=10.1007/BF01215385|jstor=25054778|s2cid=120862302|issn=0938-2259}}</ref>

=== <span class="anchor" id="komiya"></span>Polytopal KKMS theorem (Komiya) ===
[[Hidetoshi Komiya]] generalized the KKMS theorem from simplices to [[polytope]]s.<ref name=":0" /> Let ''P'' be any compact [[convex polytope]]. Let <math>\textrm{Faces}(P)</math> be the set of nonempty faces of ''P''.  A '''Komiya covering''' of ''P'' is a family of closed sets <math>\{C_F: F\in \textrm{Faces}(P)\}</math> such that for every face <math>F\in \textrm{Faces}(P)</math>:
<math display=">F\subseteq \bigcup_{G\subseteq F, ~ G \in \textrm{Faces}(P)} C_G.</math>
Komiya's theorem says that for every Komiya covering of ''P'', there is a ''balanced collection'' <math>B\subseteq \textrm{Faces}(P)</math>, such that the intersection of sets indexed by <math>B</math> is nonempty:<ref name="i81" /> 
:<math>\bigcap_{F\in B} C_F \neq \emptyset</math>
Komiya's theorem also generalizes the definition of a balanced collection: instead of requiring that there is a weight function on <math>B</math> such that the sum of weights near each vertex of ''P'' is 1, we start by choosing any set of points <math>\textbf{b} = \{b^F: F\in \textrm{Faces}(P), b^F\in F \}</math>. A collection <math>B\subseteq \textrm{Faces}(P)</math> is called ''balanced'' with respect to <math>\textbf{b}</math> iff <math>b^P \in \operatorname{conv} \{ b^F: F\in B \}</math>, that is, the point assigned to the entire polygon ''P'' is a [[convex combination]] of the points assigned to the faces in the collection ''B''.

The KKMS theorem is a special case of Komiya's theorem in which the polytope <math>P = \Delta_{n-1}</math> and <math>b^F </math> is the [[barycenter]] of the face F (in particular, <math>b^P </math> is the barycenter of <math>\Delta_{n-1}</math>, which is the point <math>(1/n, \ldots, 1/n)</math> ).

=== Boundary conditions (Musin) ===
Oleg R. Musin proved several generalizations of the KKM lemma and KKMS theorem, with boundary conditions on the coverings. The boundary conditions are related to [[homotopy]].<ref>{{cite journal|arxiv=1512.04612|last1= Musin|first1= Oleg R.|title= KKM type theorems with boundary conditions|journal= Journal of Fixed Point Theory and Applications|volume= 19|pages= 2037–2049|doi= 10.1007/s11784-016-0388-7|year= 2017|issue= 3|s2cid= 119619991}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=1505.07629|last1= Musin|first1= Oleg R.|title= Homotopy invariants of covers and KKM type lemmas|journal= Algebraic & Geometric Topology|volume= 16|issue= 3|pages= 1799–1812|year= 2016|doi= 10.2140/agt.2016.16.1799|s2cid= 119695004}}</ref>
